prompt.context: Covfefe, a Colombian coffee company, has had issues meeting its customer demand over the past few months. They have one manufacturing plant which used to be able to meet customer demand, but now for some reason they cannot. Mr. Drumpf, the CEO of Covfefe, has hired you to figure out what is going on and make a recommendation.
prompt.question: What is causing Covfefe's manufacturing plant to fall short of customer demand, and how should Covfefe recover the capacity needed to produce 75,000 more coffee bags?

clarifying_info.q: Where is the manufacturing plant located and which markets does it serve?
clarifying_info.a: The plant is in the US and only serves the US market.

clarifying_info.q: Has demand changed over the time period in question?
clarifying_info.a: Demand has been steady over the time frame considered.

clarifying_info.q: Does the shortfall affect all coffee types equally?
clarifying_info.a: Covfefe makes 5 types of coffee and all of them have very similar demand.

exhibits.title: OEE Time Breakdown
exhibits.shows: A waterfall/cascade chart breaking a 24-hour day into time buckets: Scheduled Time, Planned Downtime, Unplanned Maintenance, Unplanned Ops, Quality Loss, and Actual Performance (Running Time). All values are in hours.

exhibits.title: Planned Downtime and Unplanned Maintenance Breakdown
exhibits.shows: Two bar charts side by side. Left chart breaks Planned Downtime into three sub-categories (Breaks, Maintenance projects, Capital Projects). Right chart breaks Unplanned Maintenance into four sub-categories (Electrical Breakdowns, Mechanical Breakdowns, Other, and a fourth bar). Cycle time per coffee bag is noted at 45 seconds.

framework: Availability — was the plant running long enough? (scheduled maintenance, planned shutdowns)
Performance — of the time the plant was running, how efficiently did it operate? (unplanned downtime, machine breakdowns, operator issues)
Quality — how many coffee bags were rejected or did not meet specification?

questions.prompt: Calculate the percentage of the 24-hour day consumed by each loss bucket from Exhibit 1. Which two buckets are the biggest problems?
questions.guidance: Candidate should express each loss as a share of the 24-hour total. Planned Downtime and Unplanned Maintenance are the two largest buckets and should be the focus of investigation.

math.setup: Each loss divided by 24 hours total
math.answer: Unplanned Maintenance (20%) and Planned Downtime (15%) are the two largest loss buckets.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate how many additional coffee bags could be produced if each downtime sub-category were fully eliminated. Then identify which combination of reductions (at 50% resolution) would yield the 75,000 additional bags Covfefe needs.
questions.guidance: Candidate should convert hours to bags using 80 bags/hour (3600 s / 45 s). They should notice that 'Other' is the largest unclassified category, which should prompt curiosity. They must then identify that 100% resolution is unrealistic and that a 50% fix of Electrical, Mechanical, and Maintenance projects together reaches the 75k target.

math.setup: Step 1: Convert cycle time to throughput rate. 3600 seconds / 45 seconds per bag = 80 bags per hour. Step 2: Multiply each downtime bucket (in hours) by 80 to get extra bags at 100% resolution. Step 3: Apply 50% resolution to the selected buckets.
steps: Total at 50% resolution of three buckets: 20,800 + 30,000 + 28,000 = 78,800 bags (exceeds 75k target)
math.answer: Resolving 50% of Electrical Breakdowns (~20.8k bags), 50% of Mechanical Breakdowns (~30k bags), and 50% of Maintenance Projects (~28k bags) yields approximately 78,800 additional bags, meeting the 75,000-bag target.

brainstorming.prompt: What could be driving the large 'Other' category in Unplanned Maintenance, and what should Covfefe investigate?

categories.name: Data / Reporting Issues
ideas: Maintenance events not being logged to specific categories

categories.name: Equipment / Process
ideas: Aging equipment with failure modes not yet classified
New machinery introduced without standard maintenance codes

categories.name: People / Training
ideas: Operator errors that cause stoppages but are misclassified
Lack of trained maintenance personnel to diagnose root cause
High turnover leading to inconsistent coding practices

categories.name: External / Supply
ideas: Raw material quality issues causing stoppages
Supplier variability for coffee beans affecting processing
Utility interruptions (power, water) not captured in electrical category

recommendation: Covfefe should focus on reducing planned downtime and unplanned maintenance by at least 50%, specifically targeting: (1) Maintenance Projects, (2) Mechanical Breakdowns, and (3) Electrical Breakdowns — this combination delivers the required 75,000 additional coffee bags.
Additionally, Covfefe must immediately investigate and classify the 'Other' unplanned maintenance category (890 hours, the single largest bucket) to unlock further capacity gains.
risks: Resolving 50% of any category may be optimistic without a clear root-cause diagnosis for each bucket.
'Other' could represent systemic issues that, once classified, might require significant capital investment to fix.
Operational changes (e.g., reducing planned downtime) could create new quality or safety risks if maintenance is deferred.
next_steps: Conduct root-cause analysis on the top three unplanned maintenance sub-categories.
Immediately audit and reclassify all events logged under 'Other' to identify patterns.
Review planned downtime schedule — assess whether maintenance projects and capital projects can be batched or shortened without compromising asset reliability.
Implement a real-time OEE tracking system so plant managers can monitor losses daily.
